name: FAIR Data
title: FAIR Data
answer: FAIR Data is a set of principles for making research data Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable. It covers datasets, metadata, code, models, and the persistent identifiers that link them. In practice it applies across disciplines, from genomics to social science to AI research, and it shapes how repositories, journals, and funders expect data to be shared. A library that holds 135 research papers and 12646 extracted claims depends on FAIR practice to keep those items connected and usable. The scope is not only open data, because sensitive or restricted data can still be FAIR if access conditions are clear.

sections.body: FAIR Data is a set of principles for making research data Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable. sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The infrastructure for FAIR data includes repositories, persistent identifier services, metadata schemas, and controlled vocabularies. Common examples are DataCite and ORCID for identifiers, Dublin Core and schema.org for metadata, and domain repositories such as GenBank or a national data archive. These systems run on APIs, harvesters, and catalogues that let machines read and exchange records. Storage may be cloud or institutional, and access can be open, registered, or controlled. The point is that a person or a machine can follow a link and reach a usable record.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work is done by planning data management from the start, choosing a repository, and assigning a persistent identifier such as a DOI. Researchers write metadata that describes the data, its variables, units, methods, and provenance, often using a standard schema. They deposit the data, link it to publications, and set a license that states what others may do. Curation then checks that files open, metadata is complete, and links resolve. In AI research, this often means documenting training data, model cards, and evaluation sets so others can reproduce results.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk in FAIR data turn on consent, privacy, intellectual property, and provenance. Personal or sensitive data may need de-identification, access controls, or a data use agreement before it can be shared. Provenance records who created the data, how it was processed, and under what terms it can be reused. Licenses such as Creative Commons or Open Data Commons set permissions, but they do not settle every question about ethics or law, and repositories usually have policies for retention, takedown, and breach response. This is a description of common practice, not legal advice.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: FAIR data is moving toward machine-actionable metadata, so software agents can discover and combine datasets without human mediation. There is growing attention to the CARE principles for Indigenous data governance and to equity in who benefits from shared data. AI systems are both consumers and producers of FAIR data, which raises questions about documenting training corpora and model outputs. Repositories are adding automated checks, richer provenance, and links between papers, data, and code. The direction is toward a connected research record where data, methods, and claims can be traced and reused.
